narrative.overview:
FabricStash is a shelf you can scan in north light. The ground is cool paper, the type is soft blue-charcoal, and one sea-glass accent marks the action and the selected card. The cloth photos carry the color. The chrome stays quiet.

The brown, kraft, camel, and dark-wood studio is gone, including its serif titles and madder buttons. San Francisco (the system face) carries every label so the shelf follows the reading size the owner already set. Depth comes from a card lifted one step off the paper, not from a shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground, soft ink, one accent
The photograph is the color field of a card
A ring and a loupe mark the spot tapped on the cloth
Aligned cards, the name and the amount in the same place, spacing on a 12-point measure
Native iOS controls on iPhone and iPad, with the same palette in the browser preview

rules.name: The Cloth Carries the Color Rule
rules.body: Sea glass never tints a fabric photo or stands in for a fabric that has its own swatch. A missing photo with a sampled color shows that color. A missing color shows paper.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Sea glass is for the action and the selection. Caution is only for a problem. Nothing else gets a brand hue.

rules.name: The System Face Rule
rules.body: Labels, buttons, and titles use the platform face. A second face is not part of this shelf.

rules.name: The Flat Shelf Rule
rules.body: Do not add a drop shadow to a fabric card. The photo is the depth.

dos: Do keep the ground on cool paper and the action on sea glass.
Do let the fabric photo be the color of the card.
Do keep names, amounts, and spacing aligned from card to card.
Do use caution only when something the owner typed cannot be saved or a cut would pass zero.
donts: Don't use brown, kraft, camel, mud, dark wood, or a terracotta accent.
Don't ask the owner to type or edit a hex code.
Don't make a second photo the price of knowing the color when one photo is already on the fabric.
Don't set fabric titles in a serif.
